reason: Entries to next_a: BEQ next_a (each_b), BRA next_a (after marking a), BNE next_a (each_a) and now the copy's own BNE next_a; no table, label+N or other file references (grep: only render.6502 lines 1094-1131). Old next_a = INX; BRA each_a; each_a: CPX list_n; BEQ swept; LDY list_slot,X; LDA need,Y; BNE next_a; LDY #0; fall into each_b. New is the same instruction sequence with the BRA removed and the fall-through replaced by BRA each_b, which changes no register, flag (BRA touches none) or memory; exits to swept, next_a and each_b see identical A, X, Y, N, Z, C, V, D, list_changed, list_b, need. each_a stays for the again entry. No stack use; the IRQ sees nothing different (no writes added or reordered). Bytes: list_n is zero page (&53) so CPX 2, LDY list_slot,X abs (&B780) 3, LDA need,Y abs 3 (no zp,Y form), branches 2, LDY #0 2: 17 against 3, +14 bytes (claim -14 as a saving sign is a cost of 14). Cycles: loop-back paths drop the BRA (3 cycles, same page); the each_b path swaps the free fall-through for a BRA (0 net). Branch ranges well within 128.
